scope: Unsaturated local public-development production under the stored-compliance approximation used by the frozen marginal-return theory diagnostic.

definitions.H_i: instantaneous insurgent recruitment-hazard mass in locality i
definitions.P_i: nominal public-development capital allocated to locality i over one 30-day reference cycle
definitions.w_j: represented population of susceptible cohort j
definitions.e_j: eligible nonmember fraction of cohort j
definitions.A_j: insurgent access-strength multiplier for cohort j
definitions.sigma_l_j: logistic recruitment propensity before the access-strength multiplier

saturation.implication: The first-order ROI is locally constant only below P_sat_i. Once production reaches its clamp at 1, additional public capital has zero same-cycle marginal production/access return through this channel.

theoretical_implications: Threat alone is not a sufficient development-targeting statistic. A high-threat locality with weak capacity, reach, or compliance can have low recruitment suppression per marginal public-capital unit.

Absorptive capacity alone is also insufficient. A highly capable locality where recruitment propensity is already near zero or one has low logistic elasticity sigma*(1-sigma) and therefore low immediate anti-recruitment return.
The highest first-order anti-recruitment ROI occurs where insurgent recruitment is both exposed to the peaceful-channel margin and government institutions can convert spending into political access.

Because the recruitment-sensitivity numerator often scales with represented susceptible population while development conversion divides by locality population, population can approximately cancel. Per-capita size is therefore not generically the dominant targeting variable.

The squared compliance term makes institutional compliance especially important: halving compliance quarters the low-dose development-to-access conversion before other state differences are considered.
Development targeting should be dose-dependent. The best destination for the next unit of capital changes as high-ROI localities approach P_sat_i.

cost_normalization.usd_conversion_formula: If an external calibration later assigns B USD to the default monthly budget, then one Pineland capital unit = B/120000 USD and 1200 capital = 0.01*B USD.

guard: This is an exact/first-order identity of the implemented synthetic mechanism, not an empirical estimate of aid effectiveness or a real-world targeting recommendation.
